versions.summary: Refocuses skills and AGENTS.md on precise activation, progressive disclosure, persistent authorization, and proportionate execution using GPT-6 Astra prompting guidance.
changes: Give spec-library a short, discriminating frontmatter description with positive and negative activation cases. Keep AGENTS.md focused on durable project context, essential boundaries and commands, and a lightweight context router.

Keep the generated SKILL.md as the concise workflow entry point; move conditional discovery, HTML authoring, and execution details into references/discovery.md, references/authoring.md, and references/execution.md, loaded only when needed.

Retain repository inspection, reuse analysis, and visible documentation impact with fixed discovery minimums: at least eight material questions during init before installation edits and at least five during each activated request-refinement round before documentation-branch decisions or implementation, waiting for every answer. Missing goal or clues/examples prerequisites are additional; resume completed discovery without replaying it.

Preserve explicit choices for consequential reuse or abstraction boundaries and their canonical decision records; routine compatible reuse within authorized scope needs no separate reuse-selection question.

Preserve new-spec selection and business-spec approval, automatic existing-owner maintenance, and concrete technical approval boundaries. Earlier explicit choices and approvals remain valid for unchanged scope; documentation choices never imply unrelated implementation approval.

Scale context loading, plan detail, delegation, and testing to the task. Allow useful independent delegation when supported by the runtime and explicit local policy, without a mandatory strategy menu; retain model-agnostic capability guidance when it helps.

Complete authorized implementation, relevant verification, and document close-out without redundant approval stops, arbitrary retry limits, or repeated checks that add no evidence. Honor explicit user stop points and surface real blockers.

Focus updates on the installed SKILL.md, its references, and generated AGENTS.md guidance. Replace inherited simplest-sdd ceremony while preserving genuine user customizations, factual contracts, historical artifacts, compatibility paths, and inactive legacy data.

steps: Apply the current rules directly from every older or unversioned installation. They preserve the eight-question init and five-question request-refinement minimums while overriding repeated approval gates, compulsory execution-strategy menus, rigid context/testing requirements, and retired execution tracking; do not recreate superseded intermediate workflows or rewrite historical release notes.

Audit the installed SKILL.md and generated AGENTS.md guidance for duplicated instructions and obsolete simplest-sdd constraints. Preserve genuine user-authored policies and customizations; distinguish them from inherited framework defaults before retaining a conflicting rule.

Rewrite spec-library frontmatter with a concise description of when it should and should not activate. Reduce AGENTS.md to stable project context, essential commands and boundaries, and a precise router for workflow work versus read-only documentation questions and direct low-risk changes.

Keep activation, branch decisions, authorization boundaries, and close-out in the SKILL.md entry point. Create directly linked references/discovery.md, references/authoring.md, and references/execution.md for conditional detail; preserve HTML contracts and existing customized content while moving instructions, and load each reference only when relevant.

Preserve or restore at least eight material init questions and at least five material questions for every newly activated request, waiting for all answers before installation edits or documentation-branch decisions and implementation respectively. Goal and clues/examples prerequisites do not count; a consequential reuse choice can count toward the five. Use known facts to sharpen questions, preserve completed discovery and approvals on resume, and do not rerun bootstrap discovery during instruction migration. Retain explicit choice for consequential reuse while allowing routine compatible reuse without a separate options question.

Preserve Create a new spec versus Continue without a new spec when no owning spec exists, required approval of newly generated business specs, automatic existing-owner updates, and concrete technical approval boundaries. Recognize existing explicit authorization for unchanged scope rather than asking again; preserve approved reuse decisions in every branch without inventing historical approvals.

Replace compulsory strategy selection with task-appropriate execution under the user's authorized scope and explicit local policies. Allow useful bounded delegation when the runtime supports it, scale plan detail and executor context to actual dependencies and risks, and retain one integrated plan rather than separate task plans.

Keep the repository's resolved testing discipline and choose relevant checks for the changed behavior. Remove blanket full-context reading, irrelevant test requirements, repeated verification without new evidence, current-prompt-only authorization, and arbitrary retry stops from inherited guidance; persist through authorized implementation, verification, and close-out while honoring explicit stop points.

Validate routing examples, linked references, preserved approval boundaries, relevant verification, and absence of superseded framework rules in active instructions. Avoid bulk edits to historical specs, decisions, plans, or templates; preserve compatibility and legacy cleanup behavior. Set the schema marker to 0.17.0 only after the current workflow is present, then report changed files and rationale.

versions.summary: Improves HTML paragraph and list readability through editorial guidance, semantic inline formatting, and illustrative template examples.
changes: Direct the generated skill to make body content as readable as possible using content-aware judgment: lead with the main idea, keep paragraphs focused, and use meaningful list labels where they help readers scan.

Use strong for key clauses or meaningful list labels, em for meaningful emphasis, code for literals, and sparse mark or keyword highlights for consequential phrases; keep plain prose when sufficient and avoid deterministic keyword matching or formatting quotas.
Add concise, clearly labeled illustrative paragraphs and lists to the business, technical, plan, and decision templates; replace example facts with the actual document's content.
Add light paragraph and list spacing and semantic inline styles while preserving the existing artifact palette and accessibility.

steps: Update SKILL.md with content-aware paragraph and list readability guidance, including semantic inline emphasis, focused prose, and meaningful list labels without deterministic keyword rules or formatting quotas.

Refresh business, technical, plan, and decision templates with clearly labeled illustrative paragraphs and lists, instructions to replace their example facts, and light body and inline styles that preserve compatible custom styling, artifact colors, and accessibility.

Apply the body-readability guidance to new or intentionally revised documents. Do not bulk-rewrite historical specs or decisions; preserve factual contracts, history, approvals, anchors, and valid links.
Advance the installed workflow marker to 0.16.0. Preserve the existing discovery, approval, execution, and legacy-record cleanup behavior; this release changes presentation guidance only.

versions.summary: Removes execution records, human rating prompts, and execution telemetry; updating offers a choice to leave existing records untouched or delete only explicitly selected legacy files.
changes: Stop creating or maintaining execution.json records, human evaluations, and data/executions.jsonl; finish work after implementation, verification, and required spec and decision maintenance without asking for an execution rating or qualification.

Remove the execution schema, execution template, analytics and codex-usage commands, and active instructions, examples, links, and index columns that depend on execution records, ratings, or telemetry.

Keep task classification, estimates, capability recommendations, approved execution strategy, implementation progress, and verification in the human-readable plan without per-run model, token, timing, rating, or analytics records.

When an update finds legacy execution.json files or data/executions.jsonl, present the exact paths and one explicit choice: Leave old records untouched (Recommended, default) or Delete the identified old records; never infer deletion from the update request or a missing response.

Preserve selected legacy records byte-for-byte without parsing, validating, migrating, rewriting, or exporting them; delete only the identified files after an explicit deletion selection and remove links to deleted files without deleting spec folders, decisions, unrelated data, or other history.

Apply the current workflow directly on upgrades from every older version, overriding historical migration steps that would create, migrate, validate, export, or maintain execution records, human ratings, analytics, or codex-usage telemetry; never recreate intermediate telemetry artifacts.
Preserve discovery, documentation-branch choices, approved reuse decisions, independent technical approvals, resolved testing discipline, and historical release notes.

steps: For an update from any older or unversioned installation, apply the current workflow directly. These removal instructions override every older migration step that would create, migrate, validate, export, rebuild, or maintain execution records, human ratings, analytics, or codex-usage telemetry; do not recreate intermediate artifacts or execute obsolete telemetry commands before removing them.

Remove execution tracking, human-evaluation or qualification prompts, rating-response waits, telemetry collection, analytics rebuilds, and codex-usage instructions from the active SKILL.md, AGENTS.md workflow note, templates, examples, and close-out contract. Preserve implementation and verification reporting, spec and decision maintenance, discovery, approved reuse choices, and all independent technical approvals.

Retire generated execution templates and schema references, analytics documentation and command examples, execution-record relationship requirements, and execution or rating index columns. Remove active links to retired support files and execution records while preserving business, technical, plan, and decision content and their valid relationships.

Keep task classifications, estimates, capability recommendations, the user's approved execution strategy, progress, and verification in plan.html. Do not transfer old per-run records, model or token usage, duration, ratings, or analytics data into plans or another replacement telemetry store.

Inventory the exact legacy specs/**/execution.json and data/executions.jsonl file paths within the canonical spec library without parsing their contents or following the Claude compatibility symlink as a second library. If any exist, ask one question offering Leave old records untouched (Recommended, default) or Delete the identified old records, and display every file covered by the choice.

Do not infer deletion from the update request, the recommended default, or silence. Wait for an explicit deletion selection before deleting any old record; other update work may continue while the choice is pending, with all old records preserved. An already explicit selection covering the identified files counts and does not require a repeat question. If no old records exist, skip the cleanup question.

On Leave old records untouched, leave every legacy record and ledger byte-for-byte unchanged as inactive history. Do not parse, validate, upgrade, normalize, append to, rewrite, rename, relocate, or export them, and do not resume recording or rating them in future work. No response also leaves all old records untouched and must not be reported as an explicit user choice.

On an explicit Delete the identified old records selection, delete only the exact record and ledger files covered by that selection and remove dangling links to them from the library's documents and indexes. Never blanket-delete directories, spec folders, business.html, technical.html, plan.html, decisions, unrelated data, or other historical artifacts; resolve unclear ownership without broadening deletion.

Refresh active templates and indexes without reading archived record contents. Verify that current instructions contain no recording or rating lifecycle, no telemetry-dependent links or columns, and no command that parses or regenerates old records; preserve historical release entries as history rather than operative migration instructions.

Advance the installed workflow marker to 0.15.0 and report the files updated, the user's cleanup choice or pending/no-records status, and the exact legacy files preserved or deleted. There is no replacement execution schema or execution-record format migration.

versions.summary: Adds evidence-based reuse and abstraction analysis to discovery, records the user's approved implementation choice in specs, and preserves every approved choice in the decision registry.
changes: Inspect related implementations, actual callers, tests, and reusable lower-level logic during discovery; compare business rules, compatibility, coupling, and preservation of existing behavior before recommending reuse or an abstraction.

For viable related logic, offer reuse as-is, a separate new implementation, and a custom adaptation or shared extraction, with exactly one reasoned Recommended option; when no suitable candidate exists, document the inspected evidence without forcing artificial reuse choices.

Require an explicit implementation choice before applying reuse, isolation, adaptation, or abstraction; an existing explicit user instruction counts, unchanged approved scope needs no repeat approval, and a documentation-branch choice never implies an implementation choice.

Record the analysis, alternatives, recommendation and reason, approved user choice and custom conditions, approval status, and consequences in product language in the business spec; put exact source paths, symbols, callers, abstraction boundaries, verification, and decision links in the technical spec, with plan tasks limited to approved scope.

Persist every explicitly approved reuse-analysis choice, including keeping a separate implementation, in a canonical category decision and the decision and root indexes, even when ordinary decision-promotion heuristics would omit it or the user continues without a new spec.

Keep alternatives and unapproved ideas out of active decisions; record approved intent as pending implementation, then reconcile the decision with what shipped, including partial or unimplemented scope, at close-out.

Allow only the approved decision and necessary index writes as a narrow no-new-spec exception, alongside existing-contract maintenance; create no new feature spec, plan, execution record, or analytics record in that branch.
Preserve independent technical approval for active-decision changes and other risk gates, stricter explicit local policies, historical artifacts and approvals, and execution schema 1.1.0.

steps: Update discovery in SKILL.md to inspect related implementations, their actual callers and tests, and reusable lower-level logic; compare shared business rules, compatibility, coupling, and behavior-preservation risks before proposing reuse, adaptation, extraction, or a separate implementation.

When viable related logic exists, present reuse as-is, a separate new implementation, and a custom adaptation or shared extraction with exactly one Recommended option and its reason; document inspected evidence and limitations when no suitable candidate exists instead of inventing candidates or forced options.

Wait for the user's explicit implementation choice before implementing the proposed approach. Count an already explicit instruction as approval and avoid asking again unless scope changes; keep this choice distinct from Create a new spec versus Continue without a new spec and preserve independent technical approvals.

Extend the business template and newly created or intentionally updated business specs with product-level existing-logic analysis, alternatives, model recommendation and reason, approved user choice and custom conditions, approval status, and consequences; do not infer historical approvals or broadly rewrite old specs.

Extend the technical template with exact candidate source paths and symbols, actual callers and consumers, the approved reuse or abstraction boundary, preservation checks, and a direct canonical decision link; constrain plan tasks and acceptance checks to the approved implementation scope.

Make every explicitly approved choice from reuse analysis, including choosing isolation over reuse, a required canonical category decision with a stable ID and anchor, rationale, alternatives, approved scope and consumers, exceptions and custom conditions, approval evidence, and separate implementation state; this requirement overrides the routine inferability and cross-feature decision-promotion heuristic.

Keep unselected alternatives and unapproved ideas as analysis, never active decisions. Preserve explicit technical approval before changing an existing active decision, amend compatible decisions with history, and supersede only when the approved meaning fundamentally changes.

Record an approved choice promptly as approved intent with implementation pending, refresh decisions/index.html and the root library index, and link applicable business and technical specs to the canonical decision; approval of an approach does not certify that it has been implemented.

Permit these approved decision and necessary index writes on Continue without a new spec as a narrow exception to its artifact restrictions. Preserve required maintenance of existing contracts, but do not create a new feature spec, plan, execution record, or analytics record and do not add spec-only approval or human-evaluation steps to that branch.

At close-out in every branch, reconcile the decision and relevant indexes with the actual implementation and verification, including partial, changed, or unimplemented scope; seek approval for changed implementation scope rather than silently broadening the approved abstraction or consumers.

Update examples and validation checks for reuse, separate implementation, custom adaptation or extraction, missing candidates, prior explicit approval, and the no-new-spec decision exception; preserve stricter explicit local policies and untouched historical artifacts without invented approvals or implementation facts.
Advance the installed workflow marker to 0.14.0 while retaining execution schema 1.1.0 and its existing evaluation lifecycle; this release requires no execution-record or analytics-format migration.

versions.summary: Adds analysis-ready human evaluation to spec-backed executions while preserving legacy execution records and the no-spec branch's lightweight close-out.
changes: After implementation and verification, ask for one neutrally worded overall execution rating from 1 to 10, anchored at 1 for failed, 5 for mixed or partially successful, and 10 for excellent, plus an optional comment whenever the request has an execution record.

Preserve multiple human evaluations in one execution record, with each evaluation linked to the run IDs it covers and tracked through pending, rated, or declined status without overwriting earlier feedback.

Advance new execution records to execution schema 1.1.0 while keeping analytics compatible with legacy 1.0.0 records and representing missing historical feedback as unavailable rather than inventing it.

Persist the user's rating, optional comment, or decline before rebuilding execution analytics and refreshing the root library index so evaluation status remains inspectable with the rest of the execution facts.
Skip the evaluation prompt on the no-new-spec branch, and never infer a rating, comment, decline, or historical evaluation on the user's behalf.

steps: Update SKILL.md so a terminal spec-backed implementation with execution.json presents its implementation and verification result, asks the anchored 1-to-10 overall execution question with an optional comment, and waits for the user's response; keep the no-new-spec branch unchanged and skip the question there.

Upgrade the execution template, newly created execution records, and legacy records touched by a new execution to schema 1.1.0 with a humanEvaluations array that can preserve multiple human evaluations, the run IDs each one covers, optional comments, timestamps, and pending, rated, or declined status; leave untouched historical 1.0.0 records readable without rewriting or invented feedback.

Create the pending evaluation entry before asking, then update that same entry from the user's reply to rated or declined without guessing a score or comment; treat the reply as close-out continuation rather than a new request.

After recording the reply, rebuild the JSONL analytics ledger and refresh the root library index so the latest evaluation status and rating are visible alongside execution details, then finish that execution's close-out; route separate explicit work in the same reply as a new phase.

Update analytics validation and exports to accept execution schema 1.1.0 evaluations while continuing to read legacy 1.0.0 records; leave absent historical evaluations unavailable and never backfill inferred feedback.

Update the generated execution template, examples, validation checks, and human-facing analytics documentation to explain the anchored scale, optional comment, lifecycle, run linkage, and legacy behavior.

versions.summary: Reuses an existing owning spec automatically, asks only before creating a new spec, and makes spec and decision impact visible throughout the workflow.
changes: Inspect specs and decisions before discovery and include their exact paths or anchors in a provisional documentation-impact block with the discovery questions.
After discovery, automatically refresh an existing spec that already owns the changed behavior without requiring business-spec approval.
Automatically maintain every other existing spec whose durable contract must change, regardless of whether the user creates a new feature spec.
Ask Create a new spec versus Continue without a new spec only when no existing spec owns the behavior, with exactly one Recommended label.
Keep independent explicit technical approvals for migrations, data, auth, billing, security, public contracts, infrastructure boundaries, and active-decision changes in every branch.
Show every spec and decision consulted, used, automatically updated, or changed in discovery, approval, generated-artifact, automatic-update, and final messages.

steps: Update SKILL.md context resolution to classify an existing owning spec separately from merely related or consulted specs and decisions.
Add a provisional documentation-impact block with exact spec paths and decision anchors to the mandatory discovery message.
When an existing spec owns the behavior, update it automatically after discovery, preserve its history, report exact files changed, and do not require business-spec approval.
Automatically update other existing specs classified changed when the selected branch becomes authoritative; do not treat maintenance of an existing contract as creation of a new spec.
When no existing spec owns the behavior, ask Create a new spec versus Continue without a new spec, label exactly one option Recommended, and create a feature spec only after the user selects it.
Preserve explicit technical approvals in every branch, including the no-new-spec and automatic existing-spec branches.
Require discovery, branch-selection, approval, generated-spec, automatic-update, and final messages to distinguish specs and decisions consulted, unchanged, pending, and changed.

versions.summary: Makes discovery mandatory whenever the workflow activates, then gives the user an explicit recommended choice to create a spec or continue without one.
changes: Always run the request-refinement discovery round when the spec-library skill activates, including when the agent expects to recommend continuing without a spec.
After discovery, present Create or update a spec and Continue without a spec, label exactly one option Recommended, and wait for the user's selection.
Generate or update spec, plan, execution, decision, and index artifacts only when the user explicitly selects the spec path.

When the user continues without a spec, implement and verify the refined request directly in the current session without spec approval, execution-strategy selection, analytics recording, or artifact close-out.

steps: Update the AGENTS.md workflow note so every activated request runs mandatory discovery before any spec decision.
Update SKILL.md so it asks Create or update a spec versus Continue without a spec after discovery, labels exactly one option (Recommended), and waits for the user's selection.
Move all spec generation and updates behind the explicit spec choice; discovery answers alone must never authorize artifact creation.

Define the no-spec path as direct same-session implementation and verification with no new or changed spec-library artifacts, spec approval, execution-strategy selection, analytics record, or artifact close-out.
Preserve the existing five-minute and presentation-only activation rules, independent risk and handoff triggers, resolved testing discipline, and any stricter local gates.

versions.summary: Adds a restrained semantic color system for scannable HTML artifacts and replaces vague related links with explicit, reasoned document relationships.
changes: Give business specs, technical specs, plans, and decision documents stable artifact-specific accent colors while preserving high contrast in light and dark modes.
Add reusable status badge, keyword highlight, callout, and relationship-table styles so important contract language is easier to scan without relying on color alone.
Replace vague Related sections with Document relationships tables that identify each linked artifact's role and explain why the current document needs it.
Require direct sibling links among each feature's business, technical, and plan documents, plus the execution record from the plan.
Define when decisions, related specs, exact anchors, indexes, and external sources deserve explicit links, and prohibit links based only on topic similarity.

steps: Preserve project-customized palettes; otherwise update generated HTML templates with the semantic artifact accents, badges, restrained keyword highlights, callouts, and accessible light/dark colors.
Add data-artifact to template body elements so business, technical, plan, decision, and index documents receive a stable labeled visual identity.
Replace each template's vague Related section with a Document relationships table containing Role, Document, and Why it matters columns.
Add direct relative links among sibling business.html, technical.html, and plan.html documents; add execution.json to the plan; link decisions to exact stable anchors.
Add related specs only for a direct behavior dependency, shared contract, scope interaction, or supersession, and state the reason; do not link documents merely because their topics are similar.

Apply the new styling and relationship contract to existing active generated artifacts when ownership and link targets are clear; preserve customized or historical artifacts rather than rewriting them blindly.

versions.summary: Limits the five-minute review trigger to business or product behavior changes so presentation-only design and layout work can proceed directly.
changes: Apply the five-minute review threshold only when a request introduces or changes a business requirement, product behavior, business logic, rule, workflow, or externally observable functional outcome.
Implement purely presentational design, styling, spacing, and layout changes directly when they contain no business requirement or behavior change, regardless of review time.

Preserve independent workflow triggers for meaningful product ambiguity, expensive misunderstandings, architecture/data/auth/security/billing/public-contract risk, multi-session handoffs, behavior covered by an existing spec, and stricter local rules.

steps: Update the AGENTS.md workflow resolver so its five-minute row applies only to business requirements and product behavior changes.
Add a direct-execution row for purely presentational design, styling, spacing, or layout changes with no business requirement or behavior change, regardless of review time.
Update SKILL.md so review time alone never activates the workflow for those presentation-only changes.
Preserve all independent risk, ambiguity, handoff, existing-spec, active-decision, and stricter local gates.

versions.summary: Turns durable decisions into a small project-wide registry organized by living category documents, with explicit spec impact links and a strict preference for inference over unnecessary documentation.
changes: Keep decisions independent from feature folders in living category documents, creating a category only when its first qualifying decision is approved.
Use decisions/index.html as a compact routing page with stable decision IDs, summaries, status, dates, and direct section links.
Require each technical spec to record decisions it uses, proposes, or modifies, or explicitly state that there is no durable decision impact.
Read the decision index during context resolution and load only category documents relevant to the current request.
Create or update a decision only when it has likely cross-feature value, inconsistent interpretations would matter, and the intent cannot be reliably inferred.
Amend compatible decision changes in place with compact history; supersede only when the meaning is fundamentally reversed.
Keep active-decision changes behind explicit technical approval while allowing clearly listed new decisions to be approved with the applicable spec.

steps: Preserve all existing decisions and stable links; do not delete or blindly rewrite one-decision artifacts.
Update SKILL.md so context resolution always reads decisions/index.html, then loads only relevant populated category documents.
Make decisions/index.html a concise registry of stable IDs, titles, statuses, summaries, dates, and direct links to decision sections.
Organize new decisions in living category documents such as design.html or architecture.html, but create no empty categories and preserve older files when safe consolidation is unclear.
Add one Decision impact section to the technical template and new technical specs, listing used, proposed, and modified decisions or the standard no-impact statement.
Add the strict promotion threshold: cross-feature value, meaningful cost of inconsistent inference, and intent not reliably inferable from code, conventions, or an active spec.
Amend compatible decisions in place with compact history and a link to the changing spec; supersede only fundamental reversals.
Preserve explicit approval for active-decision changes and all stricter local approval rules.

versions.summary: Adds approval-gated execution strategy recommendations, integrated task classification, model-agnostic routing, and analysis-ready execution telemetry without fragmenting each feature's single plan.
changes: Keep one integrated plan per feature and divide it into detailed tasks classified by category, effort, risk, plan confidence, delegation confidence, dependencies, scope, verification, and STOP conditions.

Have the planner recommend same-session, delegated, or hybrid execution, always offer same-session, show a custom assignment example, and require explicit user strategy approval before spawning subagents.
Use model-agnostic capability profiles and reasoning effort for recommendations while recording the actual planner, executor, verifier, and reviewer models after execution.
Add the design category alongside feature, bug, security, performance, tests, tech-debt, migration, DX, docs, and research.
Add per-feature execution.json records plus a committed executions.jsonl ledger with actual models, tokens, duration, outcomes, revisions, verification, and user overrides.
Add read-only analytics validation/export in summary, JSON, JSONL, and CSV formats plus local Codex session usage inspection.
Require delegated writers to use isolated worktrees, review their diffs before executing changed code, and stop before merge.
Keep commits, pull requests, deployment, monitoring, and review handling outside the active phase unless explicitly requested.
Limit update prompt history to schema versions newer than the detected installation.

steps: Preserve any explicit delegation policy; otherwise update AGENTS.md so planners may recommend delegation but cannot spawn subagents before the user approves the execution strategy.
Keep each feature's single plan.html and expand it with classified task rows, dependencies, exact scope, verification, STOP conditions, capability recommendations, and user-selected assignments.
Add execution-template.json, per-feature execution.json records, and data/executions.jsonl using execution schema 1.0.0.
Add same-session as an always-available option; offer delegated and hybrid options only with planner rationale, plus a concrete custom assignment example.
Use capability profiles and effort in durable recommendations; record actual model names, tokens, duration, outcomes, verification, and overrides after execution.
Run analytics validation, rebuild executions.jsonl, and preserve old specs without inventing historical telemetry.
Use isolated worktrees for delegated writers, inspect diffs before running changed code, and never merge automatically.
Keep commits in same-session mode, merges, pull requests, deployment, monitoring, and review handling out of scope unless explicitly requested.
Use only migration history newer than the installed schema when generating update instructions.
Preserve all existing approval gates, explicit local delegation policies, and stricter execution rules.

versions.summary: Stops unconditionally installing the tdd skill and instead adapts the spec-library skill to the repository's resolved testing discipline (test-first skill, other defined testing approach, or intentional test-free stance).
changes: Remove the unconditional `npx skills add ... --skill tdd -y` install step from init.
Discover the testing discipline during inspection: explicit testing instruction, installed test-first skill, existing repo test setup, or none.
Write the resolved testing discipline by name into the generated spec-library SKILL.md implement-and-verify step so future agents reuse it.
Keep the tdd skill as one offered option when no discipline is discoverable; do not install any skill unprompted during update.
Preserve the explicit spec-approval gate; the testing discipline governs only the implementation phase.

steps: Discover the resolved testing discipline from AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/existing skills/repo test setup; do not reinstall a test-first skill if one is present.
Update .agents/skills/spec-library/SKILL.md so the implement-and-verify step references the resolved discipline by name instead of always naming the tdd skill.
Update AGENTS.md so the spec-driven workflow note says approved implementations follow the resolved testing discipline.
If a tdd skill was installed only because 0.4.0 asked for it and the repo has another explicit testing instruction, keep both but let the existing instruction take precedence.
If no discipline is discoverable, leave the skill test-discipline-agnostic and offer the init.md choice when the workflow next runs; do not install a skill unprompted during update.

versions.summary: Installs mattpocock's tdd skill as the implementation discipline and makes the spec-library skill drive implementations through it.
changes: Init install the tdd skill with the skills CLI using preselected options: npx skills add https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill tdd -y.
Update installs the tdd skill when it is missing so existing projects gain the implementation discipline.
Update the generated spec-library SKILL.md so implementations run through the tdd skill after spec approval and before product code changes.
Keep the explicit spec-approval gate; the tdd skill governs the implementation phase, not the spec phase.

steps: Run `npx skills add https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill tdd -y` in the repository root to install the tdd skill with preselected options.

Update .agents/skills/spec-library/SKILL.md so the implement-and-verify step tells the agent to use the tdd skill (red-green-refactor, agreed seams) after required spec approval and before changing product code.
Update AGENTS.md so the spec-driven workflow note mentions that approved implementations follow the tdd skill discipline.
Preserve the explicit spec-approval gate; the tdd skill only governs the implementation phase.

versions.summary: Frames the first workflow questions as request refinement and makes generated spec approval an explicit implementation gate.
changes: Rename the feature workflow's first question round from general clarification to request refinement.
State that the first questions exist to sharpen the request into an approvable spec, not to begin implementation.
Require the agent to generate or update the feature spec after the request-refinement answers.
Require the agent to stop after generating the spec and wait for explicit approval before implementation.
Keep technical approval required for migrations, auth, billing, security, public contracts, infrastructure boundaries, and active decision changes.

steps: Update AGENTS.md spec-driven workflow wording so the mandatory question round is described as request refinement.
Update .agents/skills/spec-library/SKILL.md so the first questions explicitly refine the request into a generated spec.
Ensure the skill requires the agent to stop after generating or updating the spec and wait for explicit approval before implementation.
Preserve the existing technical approval gate for high-risk technical areas and active decision changes.
Update templates or local examples only where they imply that implementation can begin immediately after clarification answers.

versions.summary: Adds a root spec-library index as the human and agent entry point for all internal specification documentation.
changes: Create .agents/skills/spec-library/index.html as the top-level library index.
Keep specs/index.html and decisions/index.html as focused supporting indexes.
Make the root library index list all internal spec-library documentation while exposing latest documents by last-updated date.
Allow small client-side filtering or search in the root library index while keeping artifacts static and readable without routing.
Require close-out to update the root library index along with spec and decision indexes.
Keep root library index links internal; internal documents may reference external URLs when useful.

steps: Inspect the existing spec and decision indexes plus all generated spec-library artifacts before editing.
Create .agents/skills/spec-library/index.html if it is missing, preserving any existing local library landing page if present.
Populate the root library index with links to all internal specs, plans, decisions, templates only when useful, and supporting indexes.
Add an accessible latest-documents section ordered by each artifact's last-updated metadata or the best available maintained date.
Keep links in the root library index internal to the repository documentation; let linked internal documents cite external URLs as needed.
Update SKILL.md so resolve-context and close-out steps require maintaining the root library index.
Add or preserve small client-side filtering/search only when it improves reading the library and the page remains useful without routing.

versions.summary: Initial versioned simplest-sdd schema with npx CLI prompts and Claude import compatibility.
changes: Record the simplest-sdd schema version in .agents/skills/spec-library/SKILL.md.
Use AGENTS.md as the canonical agent instruction source.
Use a regular CLAUDE.md file containing @AGENTS.md instead of making CLAUDE.md a symlink.
Keep .agents/skills/spec-library as the canonical skill and .claude/skills/spec-library as a relative symlink for Claude skill discovery.
Use clean static HTML for generated specs, plans, decisions, indexes, and templates.
Document the HTML readability and focus-style contract inside the generated skill.
Ship init, update, and remove agent-instruction prompts through an npx-friendly CLI.

steps: Inspect AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/skills/spec-library, and .claude/skills/spec-library before editing.
